parent: cell-37-index-split (process_seedv_raw_files_with_mne_from_drive.ipynb, cell 37: trainList/testList plus a shuffle=False train_test_split(val))
experiment: Applied the audit's retained improvement as a stdlib-only module, seedv_split.py, plus pytest tests and a root-level regression test. Read-only validation re-derived the parent split from the committed notebook JSON (sha256 35d98aa4...a5142fc; parsed, never executed) and re-measured parent vs candidate in pure Python. The candidate's structural contract (non-empty, pairwise disjoint, exact-once coverage, whole-session integrity) was checked on a grid of 160 (n_sessions, trials_per_session) inputs and compared with the parent over N=0..1000. Wall clock was measured with time.perf_counter, best of 5, at the goal's input size (48 sessions x 12 trials = 576) and at n=100000 for continuity with the prior audit. Repeated and cross-process outputs were compared by SHA-256 of the returned lists.

result.improvement: Seeded, whole-session, pairwise-disjoint train/validation/test partition: largest-remainder session quotas with a min-one-session-per-partition repair, whole sessions shuffled by a local random.Random(seed), fail-fast structural guard (RuntimeError) and a public validate_partition (ValueError) that makes 'overlapping sessions' observable. Extracted from the audit's retained cell-37 repair into seedv_split.py without modifying the notebook.
result.expected_effect: At the recorded 48x12 layout the split becomes 348/120/108 over 29/10/9 whole sessions: three non-empty, pairwise-disjoint sets whose union is exactly range(576), with no session block straddling partitions. This replaces a split in which test (461..575) is a 115/115 subset of val (460..575) and block 456..467 straddles train/val. The replacement passes the non-vacuous contract on 160/160 measured inputs; the parent passes 0/1001 with the same non-emptiness requirement (6/1001 under the audit's weaker disjointness+coverage-only contract). Cost at the goal size is 0.0758 ms best of 5 and 42.9 KiB peak traced memory, so the repair is free at this scale.

evidence: Notebook validation was read-only: process_seedv_raw_files_with_mne_from_drive.ipynb sha256=35d98aa40078b0e6a60b65cf79e2f206827468bb95f1196deeff564cda5142fc before and after; parsed as JSON only (43 cells, 33 code, every execution_count null). No cell was executed, no data was mounted, no pipeline re-run.

Committed parent literals re-derived in pure Python: train_samples=floor(0.8*576)=460; testList=range(461,576) gives test=461..575 (115); train_test_split(range(576), test_size=0.2, shuffle=False) gives val=460..575 (116). Overlap test&val = 115/115 = 100% of test; val-minus-test = {460}. 460 mod 12 = 4, so session block 456..467 straddles train/validation.

Candidate at the goal input size (48 sessions x 12 trials, seed 42): train=348 (29 sessions), val=120 (10 sessions), test=108 (9 sessions). Pairwise intersections empty; sorted(train+val+test)==range(576); every session block of 12 indices lies entirely in one partition. This reproduces the prior audit's recorded 348/120/108 exactly.

Contract over the correctness range: candidate passes 160/160 inputs (n_sessions 3..59 at trials_per_session 1 and 2; n_sessions 3..48 at trials_per_session 12) under non-empty + disjoint + exact coverage + whole-session integrity. Parent passes 6/1001 over N=0..1000 under the audit's disjointness+coverage-only contract, and 0/1001 once non-emptiness is required, so the audit's '1001/1001' figure was partly vacuous (empty val/test partitions counted as passes).

Determinism: repeated calls with seed=42 are element-wise identical; the SHA-256 of the serialized (train, val, test) lists at 48x12 is 1b8bc0aaeee1afb6055359e283e3a4625887e84082bfa1fef44b1f0285a612e8 under PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 12345, so the result is cross-process stable. seed=7 yields a different partition (different test membership). random.getstate() is unchanged across calls, and interleaving seed=7 does not perturb the seed=42 result.

Timing (time.perf_counter, best of 5, this machine): n=576 parent construction 0.0042 ms, candidate 0.0758 ms (median 0.0767), i.e. about 18x slower but still under 0.1 ms. For continuity with the audit at n=100000 (2500x40): parent 0.8738 ms, candidate 10.5176 ms (median 10.8467). Peak traced memory for the candidate at n=576 is 42.9 KiB. The ratio is not offered as correctness evidence and is machine-specific.

Ratio and input hardening measured: NaN accepted by a naive abs(sum-1)>1e-9 check is rejected here (isfinite check first); (0.7,0.2,0.1) and (0.3,0.35,0.35), whose float sums are 0.9999999999999999, are accepted via math.fsum with 1e-9 tolerance; (1.2,-0.1,-0.1), (0.0,0.5,0.5), (1.0,0.0,0.0), bool/float counts and n_sessions<3 all raise ValueError. (0.7,0.2,0.1) at 48x12 gives 396/120/60.

Suite green under both invocation styles from the repository root: `python -m pytest -q` -> 40 passed; `pytest -q` (console script) -> 40 passed; plain `python tests/test_seedv_split.py` -> 36 passed and `python test_repro_split_disjoint.py` -> 4 passed. The tests bootstrap the repository root on sys.path, so the console-script ModuleNotFoundError the challenge measured does not occur.

Regression test bites: test_repro_split_disjoint.py reconstructs the cell-37 parent from committed literals without sklearn, asserts the 460/116/115 sizes, the 115/115 test-in-val overlap, the {460} val-only index and the 456..467 straddle, and asserts validate_partition rejects the parent. It then asserts the replacement is 348/120/108, disjoint, exact-covering, whole-session, not a subset relation, reproducible at seed 42 and different at seed 7.
